requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas` skill whose description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project, naming as signs of one a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{cite}` references in code.
rationale:
The requirement has three testable parts. A `habeas` skill must be bundled. Its description must tell agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project. That description must name four signs: a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references in code.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_is_used_at_the_start_of_any_work_in_a_habeas_project]` is marked `{test}` for `requirements.cli.overview_skill`. It covers all three parts:

- **Bundled skill:** the test reads the description through the `description` helper, which goes through `skill_md` and `skill_files`. Those helpers use `include_str!` on `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md`, so the text under test is the actual bundled skill file. I read these helpers only through ripgrep matches. I did not open `description` in full, so I assume it returns the front-matter `description:` line, as its doc comment says.
- **Start-of-any-work instruction:** the test asserts that the description starts with "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas".
- **Four signs:** the test asserts that the description contains each of the four sign phrases, with a failure message naming the missing sign. The actual `description:` line in `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` contains all four.

The test asserts the outcome directly. A description that dropped any sign or changed the opening instruction would fail it. The requirement's wording ("directives in the book" versus "in its mdBook") does not change what the test needs to check.

Whether skills are published in the package at all is covered by `requirements.cli.skill_structure` through `bundled_skills_are_five_skill_directories_each_home_to_its_topics`, which is a separate requirement. I found no gap.
